coverage.category: Broken Access Control / IDOR / authorization policies (RBAC/ABAC)
coverage.notes: Agent read every route handler in app/app.py and app/server.js and checked object ownership and role checks.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference on invoice retrieval

evidence.description: The handler loads an invoice by the path parameter invoice_id and returns it without checking that the invoice belongs to the authenticated user. No authorization decorator or ownership filter exists on this route or in a before_request hook (reviewed app/app.py in full).
evidence.sanitized_code:
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = ?", (invoice_id,))
return jsonify(cur.fetchone())

findings.impact: Any user who can reach the endpoint can enumerate invoice ids and read other customers' invoices (personal and financial data).
findings.exploitability: Trivial when invoice ids are sequential; requires only network access to the endpoint.
findings.business_impact: Exposure of customer financial data; likely reportable privacy incident.

remediation.recommendation: Scope the query to the current user (WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?) and return 404 when the invoice is not owned by the caller. Centralize the check in a reusable authorization helper.
remediation.fixed_code_example:
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?", (invoice_id, current_user.id))
row = cur.fetchone()
if row is None:
    abort(404)
remediation.security_test: With two local test users A and B, request B's invoice id as A and assert 404 and no invoice data in the body.
remediation.regression_test: Assert that A can still read A's own invoice (200, same payload as before).
remediation.verification: Run both tests; review the other object-returning routes for the same pattern.

notes: confirmed by code reading; no dynamic test executed
